item.title: Gisèle Pelicot Refused Anonymity And Made Her Trial Public
item.description: Gisèle Pelicot discovered her husband had drugged her and arranged for men to assault her for nearly a decade. She waived anonymity so the trial could be public. In December 2024, Dominique Pelicot received 20 years in prison; all 50 co-defendants were also convicted.

item.title: Erin Patterson’s Discarded Dehydrator Became Key Evidence
item.description: After Erin Patterson’s 2023 lunch in Leongatha killed three guests, police recovered a dehydrator she had dumped containing death cap mushroom residue. Convicted of three murders and one attempted murder, she was resentenced to life without parole in October 2026.

item.title: A Neighbor’s Camera Helped Find Mollie Tibbetts’s Killer
item.description: Mollie Tibbetts, a 20-year-old University of Iowa student, vanished during a run in July 2018. A neighbor’s surveillance footage led investigators to Cristhian Bahena Rivera, whose car contained her blood. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life without parole in 2021.

item.title: Her Death Looked Accidental Until The Autopsy Found Bullets
item.description: María Marta García Belsunce’s 2002 death in Argentina was initially attributed to a bathroom fall. An autopsy revealed she had been shot. After her husband’s conviction was overturned, neighbor Nicolás Pachelo was convicted in 2024 and sentenced to life; that ruling was upheld in 2025.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes Let Nathan Fielder Move In Before Prison
item.description: Convicted Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invited cameras into her home 34 days before reporting to prison in 2023. Nathan Fielder eventually moved in. His documentary with Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything, follows Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, over three years.

item.title: The Jamison Family Vanished With $32,000 Left Behind
item.description: The Jamison family disappeared in rural Oklahoma in 2009, leaving their dog, phones and $32,000 in their truck. Hunters found the couple’s and their six-year-old daughter’s remains four years later, but autopsies could not determine how they died.

item.title: Amie Harwick’s Ex Waited Hours Inside Her Home
item.description: Los Angeles therapist Amie Harwick, 38, was killed in February 2020 after her ex-boyfriend broke into her home and waited for her return. Gareth Pursehouse was convicted of first-degree murder and burglary in 2023 and sentenced to life without parole.
